speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where on your leg or hip it hurts, and did this start after any injury or fall?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain sometimes seem to radiate to the hip or groin, and does he experience any stiffness in the leg after waking up or sitting for a long time? Does the pain worsen when he twists or rotates his leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Pelvis_and_Left_Hip_X-Ray. Does the pain in your knee seem to get worse when you try to rotate your leg inward or outward?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray_Left_Hip Findings: Flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C, Blood Pressure 100/65 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 18 breaths/min. Musculoskeletal Examination: Tenderness on palpation of the left hip; pain elicited with passive motion of the hip; knee range of motion is full; Special Tests for knee instability and meniscal tear are negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: "Those X-ray findings showing flattening of the femoral head, combined with your knee pain and limp, point strongly to Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. I need to confirm the extent of the changes, so I will request additional imaging before finalizing the plan. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_of_Left_Hip. DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease."
